<u>Comment</u>: Continuing the above point, Washington suggests that, contrary to a statement in the draft EIS, habitat improvement for an endangered species will not necessarily favor all associates of its ecosystem.
Response: The point is well taken, and the sentence is omitted as an overstatement.
Comment: Washington regards the relation of man's activities to "The physical intrusion of any large animal may so disturb the nesting birds (referring to brown pelicans) that they will abandon the nest," is an overstatement of the facts representing the affect of man's presence on certain populations of animals.
Response: The reference has been removed from the revised EIS.
Comment: In the section, Mitigating Measures, Washington asks"for consideration of ecosystems involved and general measures affecting land and water," in addition to consideration of the mitigation of impacts on the economy and use.
Response: Mitigating points discussed in the EIS are determined by the mitigating measures actually provided in the legislation. The bill does not provide any mitigating measures for impacts of the action on the ecosystem. Therefore, "ecosystems...and general measures affecting land and water" are not discussed in the EIS.
